description: Gripper Gen 11: next iteration of the Generalist-matched yellow fingers, built on Opus 5.5 first, then a second pass by GPT-6 Astra. Jake (voice): 'For the next change you should be doing version 11. Once Opus 5.5 finishes it, we can give it to Astra for a pass as well.' MODEL: Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) builds it. When it's done, a second worker on GPT-6 Astra (codex harness) does a refinement pass on the same Gen 11 (keep both outputs viewable, e.g. Gen 11 Opus and Gen 11 Astra). Start from the better of Gen 9 and Gen 10. Changes: (1) inner-face ridges are very shallow grooves, about 0.5 to 1 mm deep, cut straight across the full width of the inner gripping face, finely spaced as in the photos; (2) refine the shape ever so slightly against the reference photos cad/reference/generalist_gripper_gen6_*.png (the photos are the source of truth), especially skinny, pointed tips; (3) all holes go through; (4) working open/close slider and rotation in the gallery. Build/review loop with a separate reviewer, up to 3 rounds per model.

results.identified_issue: Gen 11 = Gen 10 pipeline plus: (a) ridges() in trace_photo.py places a station every 5 px of arc along outline indices RIDGE_FROM..TIP, with the normal from a ±2 px tangent. It skips stations at turns >100° within ±5 px, and skips any whose groove bottom comes within GROOVE_PX[0]+1.5 px of the previous one (inside-corner slivers). It stops where p−n·9px leaves the polygon (1.8 mm width; 1.6 mm made a pinhole at the tip). (b) ridges2d() in gripper.scad = stripes ∩ (offset(delta=1) profile − offset(r=−depth) profile) − offset(r=0.6) holes2d, extruded through plate+2. The band MUST extend past the edge: an exact-edge band left a zero-thickness skin and sealed slits, which counted as extra genus. (c) Needle width = max(HALF·(1−f)^Q·(1+A f), 0.6 d (1−d/20px)), with Q=(1.15,1.35), A=(1.31,3.0). The tail floor must vanish away from the tip: a plain 0.45·d floor turned the beak into an arrowhead (reviewer scored it 4/10 before the fix). (d) The slot row moved 2 px further outboard in px (0.4 mm inboard in the finger), otherwise the narrower jaw breached two slots (genus 31). (e) Fixed the reversed PATCH insert (a zero-width spur at the blade root). The pivot is 27.359 mm, in poses.js. check_gripper_closure.py reports 'never touches' for Gen 11, as it does for every gen 1-10: the design keeps a 1 mm tip gap. Unverified: real groove pitch/depth (robot.png resolves ~±0.3 mm); chisel vs. symmetric beak; scale is still an assumed 0.2 mm/px.
results.summary: Built Gen 11 (Opus 5.5) from Gen 10. Fine grooves now cut straight across the whole inner face, head to tip, and the needle tip is skinnier. It passed 3 review rounds (7.5, 8, 8.5) and is in the gallery with a working slider. The Astra pass is filed as voice-72fa2b1a.
results.detailed_description:
Gen 11 is in the gallery as "Gen 11" (folder v011_generalist_fingers_opus). The open/close slider and rotation work, with the hinge entry added to poses.js.

I started from Gen 10 rather than Gen 9. You said they were nearly the same, and Gen 10 has the hole-count check, which matters once you cut ~100 grooves next to holes.

Ridges: these are now what you described. There are 99 shallow cuts, 0.5 mm deep and 0.5 mm wide, every 1.0 mm. Each one runs straight across the full thickness of the inner face, with no lip at the edges. They follow the whole gripping edge, from the head corner over the step faces to about 1.5 mm from the point. That matches the ribbed face in the robot photo. Each groove is cut square to the edge at its own spot, and stops 0.6 mm short of any hole. Grooves are skipped only at very sharp corners, or where two would pinch off a loose sliver.

Tip: it's skinnier and more pointed. The mid-blade is about as full as Gen 10, but the last few mm narrow to a needle, and the beak ends 1.6 mm thick instead of 2. I put a printability floor on it: at least 0.9 mm across 1 mm back from the point. Below that it would print as a single line and snap. The reviewer twice wanted a blunt 3–4 mm flat at the end, where the black nub sits. I kept it pointed, since that's what you asked for.

Holes: all go through. The mesh check counts exactly the 33 designed through-holes, both fingers are single watertight bodies, and they never collide from 0 to 30°.

Reviews, from a separate agent each round: r1 7.5, r2 8, r3 8.5. One slip on the way: my first r3 tip floor bulged the whole beak, the reviewer caught it, and I fixed it before the final review. compare.html shows every round over the photo.

Still open, and handed to Astra: one smooth band at the inside corner below the beak shoulder, and a low-confidence hint in the side photo that the beak tapers from one side only. I filed the Astra pass as voice-72fa2b1a in agent/ on gpt-6-astra. It copies Gen 11 into its own folder, v011b_generalist_fingers_astra, so both stay viewable.

One local-only edit: the 'Gen 11' gallery label lives in Scripts/publish_designs.py. That file was already untracked in the checkout and not mine, so I edited it in place but didn't commit it.
results.user_reply_draft: Hey Jake, Gen 11 is up in the gallery. The ridges are now shallow cuts, about half a millimetre deep and a millimetre apart, running straight across the whole width of the gripping face from the head all the way to the tip. The tips are skinnier and come to a sharper point, but stay thick enough at the very end to print without snapping. Every hole goes through, and the open/close slider works. Astra's pass on it is queued next, in its own Gen 11 Astra folder so you can compare the two.

summary: Build Gen 11 of the yellow gripper fingers from the better of Gen 9 and Gen 10, with Opus 5.5 first, then GPT-6 Astra. Add shallow full-width ridges and through-holes, match the gen6 photos, and keep both outputs viewable with working slider and rotation.
